audit.whatIsWrong: The lane read tracked cooldowns when the actual resource in this matchup is Heat.
audit.why: Junkyard Titan gives Heat on every cast: at 50% he enters Danger Zone and all three basic abilities are empowered; at 100% he Overheats and CANNOT CAST for a few seconds. "Trade when his shield is down" is much weaker advice than "read the Heat bar" — the bar tells you both when he is dangerous and when he is helpless.
audit.corrected: early, mid and wants.you[2] now key the trade to the Heat bar and the Danger Zone / Overheat states.

audit.whatIsWrong: His ultimate was written as "His Equalizer" and given no cooldown.
audit.why: The real Riot name is The Equalizer, and it is 130/105/80s. At 130s a spent ult is a two-minute window in which he has no zoning tool at all.
audit.corrected: Name corrected and 130s added in spikes[1], mid, wants.foe[1] and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Electro Harpoon was never mentioned, despite being why his damage escalates.
audit.why: Riot's text: it slows, "reducing their Magic Resist", and "Rumble can carry 2 harpoons at a time". Two stacked harpoons mean every subsequent Flamespitter tick lands on shredded MR — which is the actual reason a long fight in his cone goes badly, and it argues for MR being worth less than simply not standing in the cone.
audit.corrected: late now names Electro Harpoon, its two charges and the MR shred.

edits.before: His Equalizer (R) is the danger — a wall of fire that zones and slows. Don't dash into a fresh Equalizer. Use your R to tank a fight, drain through his Flamespitter, and finish once he's overheated and silenced.
edits.after: The Equalizer (R) is the danger — a 130s wall of fire that damages and slows. Don't dash into a fresh one. Use your R to tank the fight, drain through Flamespitter, and finish him while Overheating locks his spells.

edits.before: Zone your dashes with Equalizer at 6
edits.after: Zone your dashes with The Equalizer

edits.before: Levels 1-2 favour you — Rumble is a melee mage with no gap-closer and weak base trades, so bully him off the wave while he has no way to punish you back. His Flamespitter chunks you if you sit in the cone, so trade at the edge of his range and eat as little of it as possible, but keep the pressure on. Manage the wave so you're not last-hitting under a heat-fed Flamespitter, and force him to spend HP or shield to farm.
edits.after: Levels 1-2 favour you — Rumble is a melee mage with no gap-closer and weak base trades, so bully him off the wave. Flamespitter (Q) burns a cone for 3 seconds and hurts far more in Danger Zone above 50% Heat, so trade at the edge of the cone and watch his Heat bar, not just his cooldowns. Manage the wave so you aren't last-hitting inside a Danger Zone Flamespitter, and force him to spend HP or Scrap Shield to farm.

edits.before: From level 3 your edge grows. You have W pull and E charges to close the gap Rumble can't escape — pull yourself onto him, land Q sweetspots, and drain while his shield and heat are down. Kite through the side of his Flamespitter cone rather than eating it head-on. At 6 respect Equalizer: never dash into a fresh wall, but once he's committed his R you can R back, tank the fire, and finish him through his silence window.
edits.after: From level 3 your edge grows. You have W pull and E charges to close a gap Rumble can't escape — pull yourself onto him, land Q sweetspots, and drain while Scrap Shield (6s) and his Heat are down. Kite through the side of the Flamespitter cone rather than eating it head-on. At 6 respect The Equalizer: never dash into a fresh wall, but once it's committed you can R back, tank the fire, and finish him during Overheat, when he cannot cast at all.

edits.before: Punish his overheat/silence and no-escape with drain uptime
edits.after: Punish Overheat, when he can't cast, with drain uptime

edits.before: Your item spike keeps you stuck to him — Rumble has no dash or dependable escape, so with Eclipse or Profane and drain up he simply can't shake you in a 1v1. Hunt his overheat windows, when his abilities lock out, and grind him down. Late game he becomes a real teamfight threat with Equalizer zoning your whole team, so priority evens out; play the sidelane to isolate him and force fights before he drops a big R.
edits.after: Your item spike keeps you stuck to him — Rumble has no dash or dependable escape, so with Eclipse or Profane and drain up he can't shake you 1v1. Hunt the Overheat windows where his spells lock out, and watch Electro Harpoon: it carries two charges and shreds your Magic Resist, so his damage ramps as they stack. Late he zones whole teams with The Equalizer, so priority evens; sidelane to isolate him.

notes: Packet flagged "His Equalizer" and "His Flamespitter" as probable wrong names: the first was genuinely wrong (The Equalizer) and is fixed; Flamespitter is a FALSE POSITIVE and correct. Aatrox's Infernal Chains (W) carries a derived "grounding" flag Riot's description does not support (drag + slow only); no grounding claim was made in this slice.
